cases.manifest_excluded_rust: Same huge nonlinear WENO5-Z reconstruction RHS (stencils/weno5_recon, repeated per face, plus the WENO3 boundary reconstruction) that hangs earthsci-ast-rs's diffsol integrator on the periodic WENO5 case (tests/conformance/simulation/advection_1d_periodic_weno5): diffsol has no dtmin/max-step fail-fast guard, so on this large nonlinear RHS it drives dt->0 without terminating instead of erroring, and no tolerance both terminates and meets the cross-binding-actuals gate. Blocked by structural analogy to weno5_D_periodic; Julia (Tsit5) and Python (LSODA) verify it. Remove once the Rust solver gains a step guard / is verified on this case.

No Rust tolerance both terminates and passes: it terminates only at reltol >= 1e-7 (looser hangs the diffsol integrator -- no dtmin/max-step guard), but at 1e-7 its temporal error exceeds the 1e-9 cross-binding-actuals tolerance vs the Julia reference; a tolerance tight enough to meet the gate hangs. Julia (Tsit5) and Python (LSODA) verify it.

Rust hangs at every tolerance tried (loosest reltol 1e-6; all three solvers Erk/Bdf/Sdirk wedge). earthsci-ast-rs's diffsol integrator has no dtmin/max-step fail-fast guard, so on this stiff / non-smooth-min-max / large-AST RHS it drives dt->0 without terminating instead of erroring. Julia (Tsit5) and Python (LSODA) solve it. Remove once the Rust solver gains a step guard.

Rust does not terminate on this case at any tolerance tried (Erk at the manifest's reltol 1e-10 down to a loosest reltol 1e-6 all wedge; observed >200s at 100% CPU with no output and no MaxStepsExceeded). The RHS is SMOOTH here (upwind1_D_lon_periodic + central_D_lat_zero_grad_bc + central_D_lev_zero_grad_bc — no min/max/limiter), so the trigger is problem SIZE, not non-smoothness: this is the largest simulation RHS in the suite (NLON=36 x NLAT=19 x NLEV=10 = 6840 cells with all three directional operators composed into one field). earthsci-ast-rs's diffsol integrator has no dtmin/max-step fail-fast guard, and its rejected substeps inside a single solver.step() are not counted against the outer max_steps cap (src/simulate.rs), so the adaptive controller drives dt->0 inside step() without ever returning to hit the guard. Julia (Tsit5) and Python (LSODA) both solve it (Python verified here, ok). The per-direction order claims are still fully covered on Rust by the three separate latlon3d convergence cases; only this combined 3-D integration driver is blocked. Remove once the Rust solver gains a dtmin/max-step fail-fast guard.
